verses.27:1: A vós, Senhor, clamarei, meu Deus, {sileas}: * {taceas}, nem eu {assimilabor} aos que descem à cova.
verses.27:2: Escutai, Senhor, a voz da minha prece, enquanto oro a vós: * enquanto {extollo} as minhas mãos para o vosso templo santo.
verses.27:3: Não me arrasteis {simul} com os pecadores: * e com os que praticam a iniquidade não me façais perecer.
verses.27:4: Dai-lhes segundo as suas obras, * e segundo a maldade das suas {adinventionum}.
verses.27:5: Porque não entenderam as obras do Senhor, {inopera}: * {destrues}, e não os edificareis.
verses.27:6: {benedictus}: * porque escutou a voz da minha prece.
verses.27:7: O Senhor é o meu {adjutor} e o meu protetor: * nele esperou o meu coração, e fui {adjutus}.
verses.27:7b: E refloresceu a minha carne: * e {voluntate} lhe darei graças.
verses.27:8: O Senhor é a força do seu povo: * e é o protetor das {salvationum} do seu Cristo.

decisions.latin: ne síleas a me: nequándo táceas a me
decisions.why: Two Latin verbs of silence, síleas … táceas, where the Greek has one verb twice (μὴ παρασιωπήσῃς … μήποτε παρασιωπήσῃς). Rule 1: the Latin's two words are kept two — 'ficar em silêncio' and 'calar-se' — a natural pair that repeats the thought as the Latin does. 'a me' in both: 'away from me', silence turned from the one who calls; 'comigo' is the Brazilian idiom for it ('ficou calado comigo': he would not speak to me). nequándo … et → 'para que não … e … não' (glossary formula, 2:12). Douay-Rheims 'be not thou silent to me: lest thou be silent to me'; Matos Soares 1932 'não sejas surdo aos meus rogos; não suceda que, calando tu …'. The Introit of the sixth Sunday after Pentecost is this verse (DO Pent06-0.txt); other Masses adapt it ('ne síleas, ne discédas a me').

options.label: não fiqueis em silêncio comigo … para que não vos caleis comigo

forms.taceas: para que não vos caleis comigo

options.note: Ruling: the Latin's two verbs, the idiom 'comigo' for 'a me'.

decisions.why: assimilári: 'be made like' (ὁμοιωθήσομαι), the future after nequándo — a consequence feared. Portuguese carries it inside the 'para que não' clause with the 'não' supplied (glossary nequándo … et). 'tornar-se semelhante' keeps the becoming of the passive. descendéntibus in lacum → 'os que descem à cova' (glossary lacus; the formula of 29:4, 87:5, 142:7b). Heard (draft 1): the Latinist, MAJOR — «Assimilábor é futuro indicativo passivo afirmativo: apresenta a assimilação … como consequência temida do silêncio divino. A tradução introduz uma segunda negação e substitui esse futuro por um subjuntivo» → ‘não suceda que vos caleis comigo, e eu serei assemelhado aos que descem à cova’; the stylist's worst line — the second colon wants too much breath → ‘para que não vos caleis comigo, nem eu me torne como os que descem à cova’. Held against the Latinist, with the stylist's ‘nem’ taken: the glossary row nequándo … et (working; 2:12, eight places) supplies the second negation because Portuguese ‘para que não A, e B’ is heard as ‘so that B’ — the feared thing wished for, a wrong first hearing; ‘nem’ is the row's ‘e não’ in one word and saves two syllables. Portuguese cannot keep a future indicative inside ‘para que não’ / ‘não suceda que’ (both govern the subjunctive); the fear is what the clause says. ‘semelhante’ kept (assimilári, the becoming like), not the stylist's ‘como’. The Latinist's wording is an option. The blind reader heard ‘descem à cova’ as dying.

options.label: me torne semelhante
options.note: Ruling: the becoming kept.

options.label: seja semelhante
options.note: Matos Soares 1932: the state, not the change.

options.label: seja comparado
options.note: 'be likened' (Douay-Rheims 'I become like'): the passive to the letter; heard as a judgment.

options.label: não suceda que vos caleis comigo, e eu serei semelhante (the Latinist)
options.note: The Latinist's future (‘assemelhado’ softened); with ‘para que não’ it reads ‘… nem eu serei semelhante’, ungrammatical — it needs his ‘não suceda que’ for the first half too.

decisions.latin: dum extóllo manus meas ad templum sanctum tuum
decisions.why: extóllere → erguer (glossary, open; the row names 27:2 'extóllo manus meas'), apart from leváre → levantar and eleváre → elevar. The same verb returns in 27:9 'extólle illos' → 'erguei-os', so the psalm's two places sound alike. 'ergo' (first person) is a plain present of erguer, though it looks like the Latin conjunction on the page. templum sanctum tuum → 'o vosso templo santo' (formula 5:8b). Douay-Rheims 'when I lift up my hands'; Matos Soares 1932 'quando levanto'.

options.label: ergo
options.note: Ruling: the glossary's verb, one with 27:9.

options.label: levanto
options.note: Matos Soares 1932: leváre's word.

options.label: elevo
options.note: eleváre's word (140:2 'elevátio manuum meárum').

decisions.latin: Ne simul trahas me cum peccatóribus
decisions.why: simul → juntos (glossary, open). Here 'simul … cum' is 'together with', said of one person ('me'): 'juntos' would have to agree with a plural it lacks. 'juntamente com' is the row's option (Matos Soares 1932 in Ps 52) and the Portuguese for the adverb with 'cum'. The Latin has 'me' where the Greek has τὴν ψυχήν μου; the Latin is followed. trahere → arrastar. Douay-Rheims 'Draw me not away together with the wicked'; Matos Soares 1932 'Não me arrastes juntamente com os pecadores'.

options.label: juntamente
options.note: Ruling: the row's option, which the singular object needs.

options.label: juntos
options.note: The row's word: a plural adjective with no plural to agree with ('Não me arrasteis juntos').

decisions.latin: Qui loquúntur pacem cum próximo suo
decisions.why: The relative hangs on 27:3's 'operántibus iniquitátem' across DO's line break. A prayed verse that opened 'Que com o seu próximo falam de paz' would be heard as a wish ('May they speak …'). 'Os que' makes it an apposition that stands alone and is heard at once as the evildoers of 27:3. próximo is a proparoxytone: the glossary row próximus asks for a word after it at a cadence, so the phrase goes before the verb and the mediant falls on 'paz'. Matos Soares 1932 'os quais falam de paz com o seu próximo'.

options.label: Os que
options.note: Ruling: an apposition that stands alone.

options.label: Os quais
options.note: Matos Soares 1932: bookish.

options.label: Que
options.note: The Latin's bare relative: heard as a wish.

decisions.why: 'speak peace' (λαλούντων εἰρήνην): peace as the object of speaking. The glossary has kept such objects bare ('falar mentira', 16:9b 'falou soberba'), but 'falar paz' is not said in Portuguese; 'falar de paz' is (Matos Soares 1932), and it keeps the word. The irony — peace on the lips, evils in the heart — stays.

options.label: de paz
options.note: Ruling: the idiom, the noun kept.

options.label: paz
options.note: The bare object as 'falar mentira': not said.

decisions.why: Verbless in the Latin ('but evils in their hearts'). A verb is supplied (D2): 'há'. mala is plural and concrete → 'males'. Order: 'mas há males nos seus corações' ends on an oxytone. Douay-Rheims 'but evils are in their hearts'; Matos Soares 1932 'e nos seus corações só cuidam em fazer mal' (explains). Heard (draft 1): the stylist — after ‘Os que … falam’, ‘há males’ leaves the build hanging → ‘mas têm males nos seus corações’. Taken: the verb supplied (D2) now keeps the subject of the colon, so the opposition is heard; eórum stays in ‘nos seus corações’, and the blind reader heard the hearts as the talkers'. ‘há’ is an option.

decisions.why: adinvéntio: 'invention, device' (L&S; ἐπιτηδεύματα, pursuits, practices). Six lines in the psalter (grep): 27:4, 76:13 (God's: 'et in adinventiónibus tuis exercébor'), 80:13, 98:8, 105:29, 105:39 — so it must serve God's works as well as men's schemes, and 'maquinações' or 'tramas' (only evil) cannot. 'invenções' keeps the Latin's word and serves both; the evil is in 'maldade'. nequítia → maldade (glossary; the row names 27:4). Douay-Rheims 'the wickedness of their inventions'; Matos Soares 1932 'a malignidade dos seus projectos'.

options.label: invenções
options.note: Ruling: the Latin's word; it serves 76:13 too.

options.label: maquinações
options.note: Only evil: cannot serve 76:13.

options.label: projetos
options.note: Matos Soares 1932: modern and flat.

decisions.latin: Secúndum ópera mánuum eórum tríbue illis
decisions.why: The Latin builds a chiasm with 27:4 (Da illis secúndum … / secúndum … tríbue illis). tríbuere → dar, as 'da' (15:7 'que me deu entendimento'): the Greek has δός in both places, so the Latin's two verbs are one in its source (D15's test). Natural order puts the verb first ('Dai-lhes segundo as obras das suas mãos'), which repeats 27:4's opening; the Latin's order ends the colon on 'dai-lhes'. Ruling: natural order (D2) — the repeated opening is a repetition the Latin almost has.

options.label: Dai-lhes segundo as obras das suas mãos

forms.tribue: Dai-lhes segundo as obras das suas mãos

options.note: Ruling: natural order.

options.label: Segundo as obras das suas mãos dai-lhes

forms.tribue: Segundo as obras das suas mãos dai-lhes

options.note: The Latin's order and chiasm.

decisions.why: réddere → pagar (glossary; the row names 27:4 'redde retributiónem'); retribútio → retribuição (glossary). The cognate verb 'retribuí-lhes' fails rule 3 ('retribuí' = 'I repaid', the row retribúere at the vós imperative). 'deles' for eórum, so that it is not heard as God's. Douay-Rheims 'render to them their reward'; Matos Soares 1932 'dá-lhes a recompensa que merecem' (explains). Heard (draft 1): the stylist — «“Lhes […] deles” pesa na boca, e “pagar a retribuição” soa burocrático» → ‘retribuí-lhes a sua retribuição’. Refused: ‘retribuí’ is also ‘I repaid’ (the row retribúere at the vós imperative, rule 3), and réddere → pagar is the glossary's, which names this verse; ‘deles’ keeps eórum from being heard as God's (‘a sua’ beside a ‘vós’ address is heard as ‘your’ by many). The blind reader heard the punishment due to them — the sense. His line is an option.

options.label: pagai-lhes a retribuição deles
options.note: Ruling: the glossary's two words.

options.label: dai-lhes a paga que merecem
options.note: Matos Soares 1932's sense: explains.

options.label: retribuí-lhes a sua retribuição
options.note: The stylist's words: the root twice, but ‘retribuí’ = ‘I repaid’ (rule 3).

decisions.why: 'and into the works of his hands' (καὶ εἰς τὰ ἔργα): the second object of 'understand' takes 'in' (they did not look into, perceive). Portuguese 'entender' takes a direct object; 'nem as obras das suas mãos' keeps the second object and the negation, and loses only the preposition — grammar. 'e nas obras das suas mãos' (the letter) runs into the next colon as if it said where God will destroy them. Both Vulgate-family versions: Douay-Rheims 'and the operations of his hands', Matos Soares 1932 'nem as obras das suas mãos'.

options.label: nem as obras das suas mãos

options.note: The preposition kept: misparsed with 'vós os destruireis'.

decisions.latin: déstrues illos, et non ædificábis eos
decisions.why: The Latin turns from the Lord in the third person ('ópera Dómini … mánuum ejus') to 'you' without a word. In Portuguese 'destruireis' alone could be heard as said to the evildoers (vós is also the plural; the Ps 10:2 cost). The subject named, 'vós' (D2; the Ps 10:2 remedy). destrúere → destruir (not an imperative, glossary); ædificáre → edificar. Douay-Rheims 'thou shalt destroy them'.

options.label: vós os destruireis
options.note: Ruling: the subject named, so it is heard as said to God.

options.label: os destruireis
options.note: The Latin's hidden subject.

decisions.why: Verbless in the Latin, and so open between a statement ('Blessed is the Lord') and a wish ('Blessed be'). The glossary keeps it verbless where it can (117:26a 'Bendito o que vem', 17:47 'e bendito o meu Deus'). Matos Soares 1932 and Douay-Rheims 'Bendito seja / Blessed be' choose the wish.

options.label: Bendito o Senhor
options.note: Ruling: verbless, open as the Latin.

options.label: Bendito seja o Senhor
options.note: Both Vulgate-family versions: decides for the wish.

decisions.latin: Dóminus adjútor meus … et adjútus sum
decisions.why: adjútor → auxílio (D19, with the majors held in D24: 117:7, 118:114, 9:10, 17:3b, 18:15b); adjuváre → auxiliar ('fui auxiliado'), so the family is heard twice in the verse, as the Latin says it (adjútor … adjútus). protéctor → protetor (glossary; the row names 27:7). Matos Soares 1932 'a minha ajuda … fui ajudado'. Heard (draft 1): the Latinist, minor — ‘auxiliador’. Held (D19/D24), as in 26:9b and 29:11; the participle adjútus → ‘auxiliado’ keeps the family.

options.label: auxílio … auxiliado
options.note: Ruling: the glossary; the root twice.

options.label: auxiliador … auxiliado
options.note: The agent noun the Latinist has asked for elsewhere.

options.label: ajuda … ajudado
options.note: Matos Soares 1932: splits the family from adjutórium → auxílio.

decisions.latin: et ex voluntáte mea confitébor ei
decisions.why: 'and from my will I will give him thanks' (ἐκ θελήματός μου): willingly, of my own will. volúntas → vontade (glossary). 'de minha vontade' is the Portuguese of 'ex voluntáte mea' (as 'de minha livre vontade'); 'de livre vontade' is voluntárie's (glossary, 53:8). confitéri → dar graças a (D5). Douay-Rheims 'with my will I will give praise to him'; Matos Soares 1932 'de todo o meu coração' (a paraphrase). Heard (draft 1): the stylist — «“De minha vontade” soa como uma locução incompleta» → ‘por minha própria vontade’. Taken in part: ‘de minha própria vontade’ — the idiom he asks for, with ex → ‘de’ kept (‘por minha vontade’ is also heard as ‘if it were up to me’); ‘própria’ is the Portuguese weight of the possessive in this phrase. The blind reader heard it rightly, ‘willingly’.

options.label: de minha própria vontade
options.note: Ruling (draft 2): the complete idiom (the stylist), ex → de.

options.label: de minha vontade
options.note: Draft 1. ex → de, the Latin's noun.

options.label: por minha vontade
options.note: The idiom 'por vontade própria'.

options.label: de livre vontade
options.note: voluntárie's words: merges two Latin builds.

options.label: por minha própria vontade
options.note: The stylist's words.

decisions.latin: et protéctor salvatiónum Christi sui est
decisions.why: salvátio occurs only here (grep), plural, for the Greek σωτηρίων (plural of σωτήριον) — 'the saving acts, deliverances of his Anointed'. salus / salutáre → salvação (D6); the plural is kept, as 17:51 kept 'Magníficans salútes Regis ejus' → 'as salvações do seu Rei' (glossary magnificáre). Christus → Cristo (D19; the row names 27:8). The verse ends on 'est' in the Latin; the copula is said first in Portuguese ('e é o protetor'). Douay-Rheims 'the protector of the salvation of his anointed'; Matos Soares 1932 'o protector que salva o seu ungido' (a clause). The Gradual of the sixth Sunday after Pentecost quotes it with 'salutárium' (DO Pent06-0.txt) — another text.

options.label: salvações
options.note: Ruling: the plural, as 17:51.

options.label: salvação
options.note: Douay-Rheims: the singular.

decisions.why: benedícere (God → man) → bendizer (glossary, open; D11): one verb for man blessing God and God blessing man, and this psalm has the turn inside it — 27:6 'Bendito o Senhor', 27:9 God asked to bless his inheritance. 'bendizer' with a direct object is current Portuguese; the Latin's dative (hereditáti) is not audible in either build (Ps 5:13 wrote 'bendireis ao justo'). 27:9 is sung as the versicle and response of the Preces and stands in the Te Deum ('Salvum fac pópulum tuum, Dómine, * et bénedic hereditáti tuæ. Et rege eos, * et extólle illos usque in ætérnum', DO Psalterium/Common/Prayers.txt, Special/Preces.txt) — the verse is built so that each colon stands alone as V and R. The familiar 'abençoai' is option 1 (its currency in Brazilian Te Deum singing is not verified here).

options.label: bendizei
options.note: Ruling: one verb for the psalm's turn (D11).

options.label: abençoai
options.note: The everyday verb for God blessing; the turn with 27:6 lost.

decisions.latin: et extólle illos usque in ætérnum
decisions.why: in ætérnum → para sempre (D23); 'usque' ('all the way to') adds reach. 'para todo o sempre' is the Portuguese that carries it without an added idea. 'usque in ætérnum' has four lines (27:9, 48:20, 88:4, 102:17 'ab ætérno, et usque in ætérnum', grep) and can be one formula. régere → reger ('regei-os' is safe: past 'regi'); extóllere → erguer (27:2). Douay-Rheims 'and exalt them for ever'; Matos Soares 1932 'e exalta-os por toda a eternidade'.

options.label: para todo o sempre
options.note: Ruling: usque carried by 'todo'.

options.label: para sempre
options.note: D23's phrase; usque unsaid.

choices.27:1: Ad te, Dómine, clamábo → 'A vós, Senhor, clamarei' (24:1's shape). Deus meus → 'meu Deus' (glossary). Draft 2: ‘e eu não me torne’ → ‘nem eu me torne’ (the stylist's breath; the nequándo … et row's second negation in one word).
choices.27:2: exaudíre → escutar (D3). vocem deprecatiónis meæ → 'a voz da minha prece' (D35; the row names 27:6's same words). oráre → orar (glossary).
choices.27:3: operári iniquitátem → praticar a iniquidade (glossary); pérdere → fazer perecer (D24; 27:3 is in its list). peccátor → pecador.
choices.27:4: ópera → obras (glossary). The possessives 'suas' refer to them (no other referent in the verse).
choices.27:5: intellégere → entender (glossary). ópera Dómini … ópera mánuum ejus → 'as obras do Senhor … as obras das suas mãos' (the Latin's repetition).
choices.27:6: The half-verse with 27:7 is a pair of versicles in a local office (DO Quadp1-2-OratioDNJC.txt).
choices.27:7b: reflorescere → reflorescer (only here, grep); caro → carne (the Latin's singular). The Tract of Lent III Friday and the Gradual of Pentecost XI quote 27:7 (DO Quad3-5.txt, Pent11-0.txt).
choices.27:9: Salvum fac → 'Salvai' (glossary). Latin order kept: verb, object, vocative.

audit.note: Latin = DO Psalm27.txt, twelve prayed verses (27:3b, 27:4b, 27:7b keyed by latin.readVerses for DO's double lines), no flex. No titulus (D7). DO's other uses, grep-checked (ps025/grep_do.py): 27:9 is the Preces versicle and response and the verse of the Te Deum (Psalterium/Common/Prayers.txt, Special/Preces.txt); 27:1 the Introit of Pentecost VI (with 27:8–9 in its Gradual, 'salutárium'); 27:7 in Tracts and Graduals (Quad3-5, Pent11-0, Quad6-4m1); 27:6–7 versicles of a local office.

Psalm-level draft from consult/parallels/ps027.md (Latin, LXX, WLC, Douay-Rheims, Matos Soares 1932; no Diurnal text for this psalm). DO's Portuguese not used (D12). Repeats found with ps005/grep_latin.py: adinvéntio 6 lines, salvátio 1, assimiláre 1, reflorescere 1, 'usque in ætérnum' 4, silére 3, tacére 4. Latin readings kept against the Hebrew: 27:1 'meu Deus' (not 'my rock'), 27:2 'o vosso templo santo' (not the inner sanctuary), 27:7b 'refloresceu a minha carne' and 'de minha vontade' (not 'my heart exults … with my song'), 27:8 'do seu povo' and 'as salvações do seu Cristo', 27:9 'regei-os' (the Latin's rege, not 'shepherd'). 18 decisions.

Draft 1: hard pass. Soft flags accepted: 27:1 second colon +6 (the supplied 'não' of the nequándo formula, 'me torne semelhante' for 'assimilábor', and 'os que descem à cova' — the Latin's colon is itself 22 syllables); +3/+4 in 27:2, 27:3, 27:7 ('juntamente', 'não me façais perecer' (D24), 'fui auxiliado'); −3 to −5 in 27:4, 27:4b, 27:5, 27:6, 27:9 (the Latin's long genitives and 'deprecatiónis'). Rhyme 27:3b / 27:4 'corações / invenções' at the finals: the Latin rhymes there too (eórum / ipsórum) — kept.

Draft 1. Two remarks: 27:1 MAJOR — the future indicative assimilábor made a negated subjunctive → 'não suceda que vos caleis comigo, e eu serei assemelhado aos que descem à cova'; held (glossary nequándo … et, working, 2:12: Portuguese 'para que não A, e B' is heard as wishing B; no future indicative can stand under 'para que não' / 'não suceda que'); the second 'não' now 'nem' (the stylist). 27:7 minor 'auxiliador', held (D19/D24). Marks confirmed.

audit.note: Draft 1. 17 items, 2 unknown words (iniquidade, regei-os); no wrong first hearing. Heard rightly: 'descem à cova' (dying), 27:3b the hearts the talkers', 'invenções' (schemes), 'a retribuição deles' (the punishment due), 27:5 'as obras das suas mãos' as the Lord's, 'refloresceu a minha carne' (the body's vigour), 'de minha vontade' (willingly). Latin's own openness kept: 27:5 'não os edificareis' heard as not building them up spiritually (ædificáre has both); 27:8 'salvações' plural a doubt (the Latin's plural); 'seu Cristo' heard as Jesus (D19); 27:9 'a vossa herança' heard as what God gives (hereditas → herança).

outcomes.reason: régere → reger (glossary, 2:9, 22:1); the Te Deum versicle keeps the psalter's word.

outcomes.reason: heréditas → herança (glossary); 'o vosso povo' in the same colon names it.

audit.note: ps027/revise_v2.py: 27:1 'nem eu me torne semelhante' (the second negation in one word); 27:3b 'mas têm males nos seus corações'; 27:7b 'de minha própria vontade'. Held: 27:1 the subjunctive under 'para que não' (the Latinist's major), 27:7 'auxílio'.
Draft 2: hard pass. 27:1 second colon now +5 (was +6). Rhyme 27:3b / 27:4 'corações / invenções' — as draft 1, the Latin's plurals at both ends (córdibus / adinventiónum); accepted.

Gate on draft 2: **not clean — two majors held on purpose.** 27:1 the same MAJOR on 'nem eu me torne' (the affirmative future assimilábor made a negated subjunctive; his fix 'não suceda que vos caleis comigo, e eu serei semelhante aos que descem à cova'); 27:7 'auxílio' → 'auxiliador', now MAJOR (minor on v1). Both held. The other draft-2 changes (27:3b 'têm males', 27:7b 'de minha própria vontade') passed. Marks confirmed.

outcomes.remark: 'nem eu me torne' turns the affirmative future into a negated subjunctive
outcomes.reason: Held: the glossary row nequándo … et (2:12); without the negation the feared likeness is heard as wished for; 'para que não' / 'não suceda que' govern the subjunctive, and his mixed 'não suceda que … e eu serei' is not Portuguese syntax a hearer can follow. His wording recorded as an option.
